name: fjall (pure-Rust LSM-tree)
baseline: RocksDB through rust-rocksdb 0.22, with an LRU block cache and bloom filters
verdict_reason: In redb's third-party comparison fjall 2.11 beat RocksDB on batch writes (1.28x), random reads (1.34x) and removals (1.15x), but was slower on bulk load and durable single-row commits, and compacted to 2.2x RocksDB's size. Fjall's own 3.0 benchmarks exist only as charts; its text backs a large build-time and binary-size advantage.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark (redb's author) with public source, pinned toolchain, and stated CPU and SSD.
claimed_speedup: vs RocksDB: batch writes 353 vs 451 ms (1.28x), random reads 2177 vs 2911 ms (1.34x), removals 6004 vs 6900 ms (1.15x); slower on bulk load (18619 vs 13969 ms) and individual writes (3488 vs 2432 ms); compacted size 1000.95 MiB vs 454.71 MiB. Build: about 3.5s and a ~2.2 MB binary vs around 40s and ~12 MB for a RocksDB hello-world (ratios derived from page data).
workload: 5 million random 24-byte keys with 150-byte values: bulk load, 1,000 durable single-insert transactions, 100 batches of 1,000, 1 million random reads, removals; 4 GB cache.
toolchain: rustc 1.89, fjall 2.11, rocksdb crate 0.22, cargo bench release profile
platforms: Any Rust target with a file system; single process per database
one_liner: Pure-Rust LSM-tree engine; beats RocksDB on batch writes and reads in one comparison, builds in seconds, compacts worse.
how_it_is_fast: Writes go to a journal and memtable and are flushed as sorted, LZ4-compressed tables, so batched writes are sequential I/O. Fjall 3 adds blocks with embedded binary-search indexes and optional hash indexes so cached reads skip deserialization. Being about 42k lines of Rust, it compiles far faster than RocksDB's C++.
use_it_when: Write-heavy or batch-ingest embedded storage where you want an LSM without a C++ build
Build time and binary size matter (CI, small containers)
skip_it_when: Many small durable commits: redb and LMDB were faster
Disk space after compaction matters: RocksDB compacted to less than half fjall's size
Several processes must open the same database
caveats: The third-party numbers are for fjall 2.11; fjall 3 (January 2026) reworked the block format and has not been rerun in redb's README
Fjall's own benchmarks for 3.0 are published only as charts
tradeoffs: Default durability flushes to OS buffers, not disk, like RocksDB; call persist for fsync
Fewer features than RocksDB (no merge operator or range deletes yet)
